items.title: Presentation by M/s UPL Ltd., regarding for the application of S-Metolachlor Technical u/s 9(3) TIM.
items.decision: RC recalled its decision taken in its 472nd Meeting under Agenda Item No. 10.43, wherein the applicant was directed to make a detailed presentation before the Committee for further consideration. Accordingly, M/s UPL Limited made a presentation before the Committee and submitted, inter alia, that the toxicological profiles and impurity profiles of S-Metolachlor and Metolachlor are comparable and proposed that the available toxicity data on Metolachlor may be considered for the safety assessment of S-Metolachlor based on the bridging rationale. The Committee deliberated upon the submissions made by the applicant. After due consideration, the Committee directed the applicant to submit the requisite toxicity data in accordance with the prescribed guideline applicable to registration under Section 9(3) TIM. The matter may accordingly be considered further upon submission and evaluation of the requisite toxicity data in accordance with the applicable requirements.

items.title: Representation received from stakeholders for revisiting the Registration requirement and the modalities for grant of registrations under "Export Only" and "Import for Export" categories.
items.decision: RC deliberated the agenda in details and observed that the requested guidelines use to be in existence and formulated in 347th RC which was later on revised in 380th RC meeting. The RC was of the opinion that the spillage/leaching of unregistered molecules may infiltrate into Indian market, so before deciding on the guidelines it was felt appropriate that Crop Life India may be asked for a detailed presentation regarding the changes proposed along with the present provisions under which the export certificates for Import for Export on unregistered molecules category are received from unregistered source and suggest SOP/procedure/conditions to contain/regulate while avoiding Indian market access/use. RC also directed them to present details about the issues encountered wrt to the present guidelines for Export u/s 9(3).

items.title: Confirmation of Data Verification/Generation by concerned institutes/labs submitted along with the application for registration of insecticide. In continuation to the decision taken in its 468th meeting vide agenda item no. 3.1, RC again reiterated that the need for verification of data/reports pertaining to various toxicity or other studies generated in NABL/GLP conditions may be taken on case-to-case basis for ascertaining the authenticity of the studies comprehensively by the Sectt. of CIB&RC. items.decision: RC decided that a team of one expert from Sectt. of CIB&RC and one officers nominated by the NGCMA in case of GLP and a team of two officers from the Sectt. of CIB&RC in case of NABL may be deputed as and when needs arise on-site evaluation of study-specific data/reports.

items.title: Consideration of an application of M/s PI Industries Ltd. for grant of registration for indigenous manufacture of Pioxaniliprole Technical 97.5% w/w min. under section 9(3) TIM of the Insecticide Act, 1968.
items.decision: RC deliberated the agenda and considered the application of Pioxaniliprole Technical (97.5% w/w min.) U/S 9(3) of the Insecticides Act, 1968 in TIM category. The RC was informed that the applicant has claimed that this molecule is invented and ready for launch in India even before registration in any other country of the world. This molecule has been scrutinized as per the definition of New Molecule decided in 434th Meeting held on 30.11.2021 and under "Make in India" initiatives approved by the RC in its 437th Meeting held on 16.03.2022. The Committee observed that Pioxaniliprole is the first insecticide active ingredient discovered in India; applied for registration under Section 9(3) of the Insecticides under TIM and FIM category. The Committee noted that the present application gives practical effect to its aforesaid decisions on indigenous capability in crop protection chemicals and is in consonance with the objective of the Government of India of promoting research and development within the country and the development of indigenous technologies for the benefit of the Indian farmer. The RC decided to approve for grant of registration for Technical Indigenous manufacture of Pioxaniliprole Technical 97.5% w/w min. under section 9(3), with a provisional shelf life of two years. The following condition may also be incorporated in the CR or L/L wherever applicable: “The applicant is required to submit real time / actual storage stability study data in the proposed construct and container of sale for duration of minimum 30 months, within two and half years of submission of application for granting the registration, failing which Registration Certificate shall be deemed cancelled.”

items.title: Consideration of application of M/s Saraswati Agrochemcials India Pvt. Ltd., for grant of registration of Formetanate hydrochloride Technical 92% w/w Min. for import under section 9(3) TI of the Insecticide Act, 1968.
items.decision: RC discussed and deliberated the agenda in details and observed that various issues pertaining to the application needs to be addressed properly. Therefore, the RC feels expedient to call the applicant to make a presentation in the next RC meeting on the following points of concern on Formetanate hydrochloride: 1. Formetanate hydrochloride belong to WHO classification by hazard category 1b i.e. highly hazardous pesticide. Since the molecule belong to bright red colour toxicity triangle pesticide, absolute necessity may be justified. 2. The nitrosamine impurity N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) which seems to be a probable carcinogen, which may arise from the presence of the N-dimethylamino group, has not been disclosed in the chemical composition. Furthermore, this impurity may also form during storage and also in field. 3. The toxicology studies submitted by the applicant have been sponsored by various companies and none of these studies was sponsored by the proposed manufacturer i.e. Sunko Ink co Ltd, Taiwan. Therefore, the applicant is required to establish the linkage between the respective study sponsors and the proposed manufacturer through authorization. 4. Purity of technical material used to conduct acute inhalation toxicity study, skin sensitization study, repeated dose dermal toxicity study is below the proposed minimum purity of 92%. 5. Chemical composition of the technical material used in teratology study of rat, unscheduled DNA Repair in cultured mammalian cells and mouse lymphoma assay is different from the proposed chemical composition in Form 1. 6. Waiver request for repeated dose inhalation toxicity study need justification keeping in view the following: a) Formetanate hydrochloride is highly toxic by the inhalation route, with an acute inhalation LC50 of 0.15 mg/l. b) Lungs are the highly vascular organ due massive surface area and thin epithelial lining. Therefore, chemical absorbed through this route can rapidly enter the systemic circulation, potentially resulting in systemic toxicity. c) Formetanate hydrochloride is highly water soluble and dissolve readily in respiratory tract lining fluids and alveolar surfactant. Hence, absorbs rapidly. d) Repeated inhalation exposure may cause persistent and cumulative pulmonary effects like inflammation, tissue injury or fibrosis. 7. Waiver request for developmental and delayed neurotoxicity study need justification considering it is a mandatory requirement for pesticides classified as neurotoxicants, particularly in view of the pesticide’s proposed mode of action and recurrent findings of neurotoxicity observed in sub-chronic and chronic studies. 8. Formetanate hydrochloride is a water soluble N-methylcarbamate insecticide that may pose high potential risk for leaching into soil and contaminate groundwater. Potential risk of Ground water contamination keeping in view its proposed label claims on onion and chilli and major metabolites of plant/soil/water. 9. items.title: Follow up of agenda item no. 10.13 of 470 RC meeting pertaining to the compliance of order dated 06.02.2026 passed by the Appellate Authority in revision petition no. 03 of 2025 M/s. Shobikaa v/s CIB&RC in FIM vs FI Deltamethrin LLIN matter.
items.decision: RC perused the agenda and at the outset observed that the above matter is being dealt on the directions of the Appellate Authority passed in Revision Petition No 03 of 2025 vide Order dated 06.02.2026 mentioning that the gamut of technical aspects involved in the matter are also required to be re-examined by the RC and in case of requirement, a consultative process may be adopted with ICMR, the apex body for framing the protocols w.r.t evaluation of public health Insecticides having adequate technical competence. In such situation, the petitioner shall also be at liberty to present their point of view. Subsequently, the matter was placed in the 470th RC meeting held on 23.03.2026 (Vide agenda item no. 10.13). The decided as under: "RC deliberated the agenda in detail and directed the Secretary, CIB&RC to discuss the issues with the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) strictly as per the observations of Hon’ble Appellate Authority in its order dated 06.02.2026 at the level of Secretariat of CIB&RC. The copy of the order is also to be shared with ICMR. The concerned bio efficacy expert is directed to submit the detailed report to the Registration Committee for further deliberations". In order to comply with the order passed by the Hon’ble Appellate Authority on 06th February 2026 and the decision of 470th RC meeting, the Secretary, Central Insecticide Board and Registration Committee (CIB&RC) convened a meeting with the Scientists of ICMR & NIMR in the Secretariat of CIB&RC, Faridabad. During the meeting, the Scientists from ICMR and NIMR informed that the matter needs to be discussed in the ICMR- Expert group on Evaluation of Vector Control Products (EVCP). RC also observes that since the comments from the ICMR were awaited and therefore the RC could not take a final decision in the matter within the stipulated timelines. The bio-efficacy expert informed that the ICMR had now submitted their inputs in the matter in terms of consultative process adopted by the RC with ICMR. RC also perused the letter dated 08.09.2026 issued by Dr. Nivedita Gupta, Scientist- G, ICMR addressed to Secretary, CIB&RC. In terms of the observations made by the Hon’ble Appellate Authority, the aforesaid inputs provided by the ICMR must also be shared with M/s Shobikaa Impex Pvt. Ltd., the petitioner in the matter to also present their response thereto. RC accordingly decided and directs the concerned bio-efficacy expert to share the complete communication dated 08.09.2026 received from the ICMR to M/s Shobikaa Impex Pvt Ltd. Further the Secretariate of CIB&RC is directed to invite M/s Shobikaa Impex Pvt. Ltd. in the next RC meeting to make a presentation in this regard so as to enable the RC to take a final view in the matter in terms of the observations and directions made by the Hon’ble Appellate Authority in its order dated 06.02.2026.

(iii) Framing of Guidelines on Insecticides/Fungicides with a pack of surfactant to reduce the load of the pesticides in to the environment.

items.title: Reducing the pendency of bio-pesticides applications and analysis of 16Sr DNA finger printing from NBAIM. A meeting was held on 16th September 2026 among officials of Central Insecticides Board & Registration Committee (CIB&RC) and ICAR-National Bureau of Agriculturally Important Microorganisms (ICAR-NBAIM), Mau, under the chairmanship of Dr. Poonam Jasrotia, ADG (PP&B) to deliberate upon issues related to the generation, processing and submission of DNA finger printing reports of biopesticides through the CROP portal. The MOM of the above meeting has been circulated to all the RC, members presented in the meeting through email for discussion and decision. The MOM is attached as Annexure- 11.2.1. After discussion and deliberation telephonically on the issue it was decided that all the biopesticides applicants needs to submit a sample in NBAIM for 16 Sr DNA Printing and sample receipt of the same is to be uploaded into the CROP portal as a proof as per existing guidelines. It is observed that many applicants are submitting sample in NBAIM but not submitting the application in CROP portal. Therefore, it is decided to redefine the flow for filling of application of bio- pesticides as under: 1. The applicant has to submit the application of the biopesticides into the CROP portal after paying requisite fees. 2. The applicant has to submit 500 gm sample of biopesticide as per guidelines of registration in ICAR-National Bureau of Agriculturally Important Microorganisms (NBAIM), Kushmaur, Mau Nath Bhanjan 275103 (U.P.) India mentioning the application number generated in CROP portal; within 30 days from the submission of application in CROP portal. 3. The applicant has to submit 500 gm sample of biopesticide as per guidelines of registration in Central Insecticides Laboratory mentioning the application number generated in CROP portal; within 30 days from the submission of application in CROP portal. 4. A Notification for submission of receipt of samples in CIL & NBAIM will be reflected in the concerned login in CROP immediately after submission of application. 5. The applicant has to submit the sample submission receipt of CIL & NBAIM clicking on the notification shown in CROP in the respective login ID of applicants. 6. A track option for CIL and NBAIM to verify the status of submission of application at the time of submission of sample shall be created by CGG. 7. The application automatically shall be deemed rejected, in case of non- submission of receipt in prescribed time line (30) days. 8. The concerned expert has to prepare a list of such cases and putup to RC for approval of rejection.
items.decision: The RC directed the Secretary (CIB&RC) to issue a public notice for the awareness of all the stake holders and team CGG to redefined the flow of filling of application. Meeting ended with a vote of thanks to the Chair *****
